# Frontend external regression fixture

`hey_jarvis.wav` and `hey_jarvis_features.bin` are copied unchanged from
Techo5 `2b091439765d5f881de4b89255b8cf0637d80cba`,
`echod/internal/lib/mwwfront/testdata`. They also byte-match
[zserge/microwakeword at bfaf3840114ece54665c15e6e202ddb1463c3d37](https://github.com/zserge/microwakeword/tree/bfaf3840114ece54665c15e6e202ddb1463c3d37/testdata).
That repository's MIT license is included in `LICENSE-MIT.txt` (Copyright
2025 Serge Zaitsev), consistent with Techo5's NOTICE for these test fixtures.
These are test data, not release models.

The dump has a little-endian uint32 frame count (615), uint32 channel count
(40), then 24,600 signed int8 features for a 10 ms step. The regression reads
the WAV's actual data chunk and checks every supplied feature exactly. The
WAV contains 98,731 mono 16 kHz samples: 615 complete 30 ms windows at a
10 ms step, all covered by the dump.

**Provenance limitation:** neither source testdata directory contains a
README or a generation script. Techo5's test comment calls the dump
microWakeWord/pymicro-features output, but the upstream test only labels it
golden data and does not record its generator, version, settings or command.
Consequently this is an externally supplied regression fixture, not a
reproducibly generated, independently verified PCM-to-C-frontend parity
proof. No features were generated by this Go port. Reset/chunk consistency
and pinned-table tests are separate checks, not independent parity evidence.
